les: Hoe ons vandag reis en vragte vervoer
kaps_punt: algemene vorms van vervoer van mense en goedere op grond vandag

items.bewering: Die meeste kinders kom te voet, en hier en daar kom een op 'n fiets.
items.blok: Hoe mense vandag op land reis
items.bron: Stats SA, National Household Travel Survey 2020 (statssa.gov.za/?p=14054; NHTS 2020 presentation, statssa.gov.za/publications/P0320): about 63% of school-going learners walked all the way to school in 2020 (59.4% of all learners, higher education included); General Household Survey 2024 as reported by Cape Argus (28 Oct 2025): 61.1% walk, 14.8% parent-arranged transport, 10.1% private car, 7.1% taxi, 1.5% bus, with bicycles not even a listed category (at most part of the 5.4% left over). 'Die meeste' and 'hier en daar een op 'n fiets' both hold nationally. Note for a person, not a fault: the sentence comes straight after 'Kyk môreoggend na die pad wat by jou skool verbyloop', so it reads as a prediction about the learner's own school. It is true of South Africa as a whole, but at many urban and suburban schools cars and lift clubs carry most children, so some learners will look and not see what the lesson says they will.

items.bewering: Ander klim by die hoek in 'n minibus-taxi of in 'n bus.
items.blok: Hoe mense vandag op land reis
items.bron: GHS 2024 via Cape Argus (28 Oct 2025): 7.1% of learners travel to school by taxi and 1.5% by bus; Stats SA NHTS 2020 via SAnews (sanews.gov.za/node/50909): taxis are the most-used public transport mode.

items.bewering: Vir baie Suid-Afrikaners is die minibus-taxi die gewoonste manier om te reis.
items.blok: Hoe mense vandag op land reis
items.bron: Stats SA NHTS 2020 via SAnews (sanews.gov.za/node/50909): walking is the most common mode overall (17.4 million people), then taxis (10.7 million), then car as driver (6.2 million); households using taxis rose from 9.8 million in 2013 to 11.4 million in 2020. Daily Dispatch (5 Mar 2021), citing the NHTS: taxis carried 80.2% of workers who used public transport. The superlative holds because it is limited by 'vir baie': taxis are the commonest way to travel for millions of people, but not for South Africans as a whole, where walking comes first. The lesson does not claim otherwise, and its previous sentence already says most children walk.

items.bewering: In party groot stede ry mense elke dag met die trein werk toe.
items.blok: Hoe mense vandag op land reis
items.bron: Metrorail Gauteng (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metrorail_Gauteng): PRASA's Metrorail runs commuter rail in Gauteng, the Western Cape, KwaZulu-Natal and the Eastern Cape, up to two million passengers a day; Gautrain links Johannesburg, Pretoria, Ekurhuleni and OR Tambo. Engineering News (2 Dec 2022) records the steep fall in ridership, but daily commuter rail still runs, so 'party groot stede' is accurate.

items.bewering: Ander mense ry in 'n kar tot reg voor die skool se hek.
items.blok: Hoe mense vandag op land reis
items.bron: GHS 2024 via Cape Argus (28 Oct 2025): 10.1% of learners travel to school by private car and a further 14.8% by parent-arranged transport.

items.bewering: Die skoene en die suiker in 'n winkel is nie daar gemaak nie.
items.bron: SA Sugar Association (sasa.org.za/the-sugar-industry-at-a-glance): sugarcane is grown only in KwaZulu-Natal and Mpumalanga and milled at about 12 mills there, so sugar on any shop shelf was made elsewhere. Shoes are made in factories and are not produced in a shop.

items.bewering: Byna alles op die rakke moes van êrens anders af tot daar kom.
items.bron: Shoprite Holdings supply-chain fact sheet (shopriteholdings.co.za, Riverfields DC): 29 distribution centres supply its stores; IOL Business Report on Pick n Pay's move to centralised distribution: suppliers deliver to central warehouses rather than to each store. 'Byna alles' rather than 'alles' is correctly hedged, since in-store bakeries make a small share of stock on site.

items.bewering: Party vrag kom van 'n fabriek of 'n plaas hier naby.
items.bron: Shoprite fact sheet: its distribution centres are placed close to both stores and suppliers. That some goods come from local factories and farms is a hedged general statement ('party') and is uncontroversial.

items.bewering: Ander vrag kom met 'n skip by 'n hawe aan en ry van daar af verder.
items.bron: Engineering News (17 Oct 2025, white paper on an inland port for the Durban-Gauteng corridor) and World Cargo News (Nov 2013, City Deep upgrade): Durban Container Terminal handles the bulk of container freight moving in and out of Gauteng, which goes on inland by road and rail; rail moves less than 14% of that corridor's volumes.

items.bewering: Baie winkels kry hul goedere eers by 'n groot pakhuis.
items.bron: Shoprite Holdings Riverfields DC fact sheet (29 distribution centres); IOL Business Report 'Pick n Pay phases in centralised distribution': suppliers deliver to centralised warehouses, and one truck then loads mixed goods for a particular store.

items.bewering: Vragmotors ry sulke vrag dag en nag op Suid-Afrika se paaie.
items.bron: Engineering News / Creamer Media (3 Oct 2025), from Stats SA land freight data: in July 2025 more than 85% of South Africa's land freight went by road, about six tonnes by road for every tonne by rail. Trucks running around the clock on the main corridors fits that volume, and 'dag en nag' is the ordinary way of saying it.

items.bewering: Goederetreine dra swaar vragte oor lang afstande op die spore.
items.bron: Sishen-Saldanha railway line (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sishen%E2%80%93Saldanha_railway_line; Railway Journal, 'Transnet invests in heavy haul capacity'): an 861 km iron-ore line with loaded trains of up to about 41 000 tonnes; the Ermelo-Richards Bay coal line is 588 km. Engineering News (3 Oct 2025): Transnet moved about 168 million tonnes by rail in 2025/26, most of it bulk.

items.bewering: 'n Trein bly egter op sy spoor tot by die volgende stasie. 'n Vragmotor kan afdraai en die vrag tot by die winkel self bring.
items.bron: DHL Freight Connections, 'Road transport vs rail transport: head-to-head comparison': road's main strength is door-to-door service and flexibility of place, while a freight train is tied to the rail network and its terminals, so road usually carries the first and last legs; Norfolk Southern, 'First and Final Mile': trucks move freight between customer premises and the rail network. Checked as a contrast: the mapping holds (a train cannot leave its track, a truck can reach the shop door), and a learner reasoning further from it arrives at the right idea that goods come off the train and onto a truck. One looseness, not wrong enough to correct: goods trains go to freight terminals, sidings and ports and pass many stations without stopping, so 'die volgende stasie' is a simplification of 'a place on the line where it can be unloaded'.

items.bewering: Twee mense op dieselfde pad kies nie altyd dieselfde vervoer nie. Hulle vra wat 'n rit met elke soort vervoer gaan kos. Hulle kyk ook hoe ver hulle op daardie dag moet gaan. Hulle vra ook wat hulle alles moet saamdra.
items.blok: Hoekom mense nie dieselfde kies nie
items.bron: Stats SA NHTS 2020 via SAnews (sanews.gov.za/node/50909): learners mostly walked because the school was near enough, and 11.0% cited public transport being too expensive (13.1% in rural areas), so cost and distance both drive the choice; DHL Freight Connections: the load decides between modes for freight. Cost, distance and what has to be carried are all real factors in choosing transport.

items.bewering: 'n Kind wat twee strate ver skool toe gaan, loop sommer soontoe. Sy ma werk 'n uur se rit ver en klim in 'n minibus-taxi.
items.blok: Hoekom mense nie dieselfde kies nie
items.bron: Stats SA NHTS 2020: walking learners mostly walk because the school is close; Daily Maverick (4 Mar 2021, NHTS 2020): workers' average taxi commute rose from 50 minutes in 2013 to 63 minutes in 2020, so 'an hour's ride' by minibus taxi is typical, not exaggerated.

items.bewering: 'n Boer met 'n vrag sakke mielies bel iemand met 'n vragmotor.
items.blok: Hoekom mense nie dieselfde kies nie
items.bron: Engineering News (3 Oct 2025): more than 85% of land freight goes by road. An illustrative case consistent with how farm produce moves; hiring a road haulier for a load of maize bags is ordinary practice and the sentence does not claim that every farmer does it.

items.bewering: Mense op dieselfde pad het dus nie almal dieselfde nodig nie.
items.blok: Hoekom mense nie dieselfde kies nie
items.bron: A conclusion drawn from the three cases before it, which were each checked above; the mode-choice factors are supported by the NHTS 2020 reasons for travel choice (SAnews, sanews.gov.za/node/50909).

items.bewering: Nie elke nuwe soort vervoer het die ou soorte vervang nie.
items.bron: Stats SA NHTS 2020: walking is still the most common way South Africans travel (17.4 million people); Starkey, 'The donkey in South Africa: myths and misconceptions' (animaltraction.net): the donkey still provides vital transport for many rural people. Old modes clearly survive alongside new ones.

items.bewering: Mense loop vandag nog soos in die tyd voordat hulle diere vir vervoer gebruik het.
items.bron: Stats SA NHTS 2020 via SAnews: walking is the most common mode (17.4 million people); Smithsonian Magazine on donkey domestication (about 7 000 years ago) and British Museum, 'Horses and human history' (horse domestication about 3500 BC): people walked and carried loads long before animals were used for transport. The comparison maps cleanly, since walking then and now is the same activity.

items.bewering: Kinders en werkers ry vandag nog elke dag fiets op ons paaie.
items.bron: Qhubeka (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Qhubeka; UJ News on bicycles for Hanyani Secondary learners in Limpopo; News24, 31 May 2015, Eastern Cape pupils): about 110 000 bicycles given to South African learners and workers so they can ride to school and work; Qhubeka's work-to-earn programme, e.g. 380 North West health workers on bicycles. A minority mode, but daily use by both groups is documented, and the lesson does not claim many.

items.bewering: Treine ry vandag nog op spore net soos die stoomtreine van lank gelede.
items.bron: Steam locomotive (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steam_locomotive) and Amgueddfa Cymru / Museum Wales, 'Birth of the Railway Locomotive': steam locomotives ran on rails from Trevithick's Penydarren engine of 1804 and the Stockton and Darlington Railway of 1825; Metrorail and Transnet trains still run on rails today (Metrorail Gauteng, Sishen-Saldanha line). The mapping is limited to 'op spore' and makes no claim that today's trains are steam-driven, so it does not mislead.

items.bewering: Op party plekke in Suid-Afrika trek diere nog karretjies met vrag daarop.
items.bron: Starkey, 'The donkey in South Africa: myths and misconceptions', and Starkey et al., 'Animal traction in South Africa' (1995) (animaltraction.net): transport is the main use of draught animals, and donkey carts are widely used by rural people; University of Fort Hare study of 71 donkey-cart owners in Joza, Makhanda, Eastern Cape (libdspace.ufh.ac.za, 2014); Karoo Space, 'All About Karoo Donkeys', and Daily Maverick (11 Apr 2025) on donkey carts as a normal sight on Karoo roads today. South African sources, as required for a claim about local practice.

items.bewering: Eers het mense self geloop en self gedra.
items.bron: British Museum, 'Horses and human history', and Smithsonian Magazine on donkey domestication: animal transport began some 5 500 to 7 000 years ago, long after people had been walking and carrying everything themselves.

items.bewering: Daarna het diere gedra en karretjies en waens getrek.
items.bron: Berkshire Archaeology, 'The donkey in human history': donkeys were among the first animals used as pack animals and to pull wheeled vehicles; History of horse-drawn transport (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_horse-drawn_transport): wheeled carts from about 3500-3000 BC; Ox-wagon (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ox-wagon): ox wagons used in South Africa, including on the Great Trek in the 1830s and 1840s. The order pack animals, then carts and wagons, is right.

items.bewering: Die stoomenjin het treine oor lang spore getrek.
items.bron: Museum Wales, 'Birth of the Railway Locomotive' (Trevithick's Penydarren locomotive, 1804); Steam locomotive (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steam_locomotive): the Stockton and Darlington Railway, the first public railway to use steam locomotives, opened on 27 September 1825. Comes after animal-drawn carts and wagons in the list, which is correct.

items.bewering: Die fiets ry vorentoe wanneer 'n mens self trap.
items.bron: History of the bicycle (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_the_bicycle) and History.com, 'Bicycle history': Drais's draisine of 1817 had no pedals and was pushed along with the feet; pedal-driven velocipedes appeared in France in the 1860s (Michaux, Lallement), and Starley's Rover safety bicycle in 1885. The sentence describes the pedalled bicycle, so its place after the steam railway (1804/1825) and before the motor car (1886) is right. The mechanism (a person pedals and the bicycle moves forward) is correct.

items.bewering: Later het die kar met sy eie enjin gekom.
items.bron: Benz Patent-Motorwagen (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benz_Patent-Motorwagen) and National Motor Museum, '29th January 1886 – the birth of the motorcar?': Benz's patent was filed on 29 January 1886, and it is widely regarded as the first practical automobile, on sale from 1888. That comes after the steam railway and the pedal bicycle. The sentence makes no 'first' claim, so the earlier steam road carriages do not make it wrong.

items.bewering: Vandag ry die fiets, die kar en die trein nog saam met die mense wat loop. Op party plekke trek diere ook nog karretjies.
items.bron: Stats SA NHTS 2020 via SAnews and Daily Maverick (walking, car, train and taxi use in 2020); Qhubeka (bicycles); Starkey (animaltraction.net) and UFH Joza study (donkey carts). Consistent with the block 'Wat van vroeër oorgebly het', which was checked above.

items.bewering: Die meeste mense kan vandag verder en vinniger reis as die mense van vroeër.
items.bron: Ox-wagon (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ox-wagon): a usual day's distance of about 19 km for an ox team, against a taxi or bus covering that in well under an hour; Stats SA NHTS 2020 via SAnews: 10.7 million South Africans use taxis and millions more cars, buses and trains. 'Die meeste' is properly hedged (not 'alle'), and 'kan' states access rather than use, which is why it holds even though walking is still the commonest mode.

items.bewering: Baie goedere in 'n winkel kom van plekke ver buite jou dorp.
items.bron: SASA: sugar comes from only two provinces; Engineering News (17 Oct 2025): imported goods arrive through Durban and go inland; Shoprite fact sheet: national network of distribution centres.

items.bewering: 'n Mens se werk hoef ook nie meer naby sy huis te wees nie.
items.bron: Daily Maverick (4 Mar 2021, NHTS 2020): 43.5% of workers commute by private car and 35% by public transport, with average taxi commutes of 63 minutes and train commutes of 107 minutes, so many people work far from where they live.

items.bewering: minibus-taxi: 'n Klein bus wat mense teen 'n prys ry en vertrek wanneer hy vol is.
items.bron: Mokwena, 'Measuring how long passengers wait to depart in minibus taxis', Southern African Transport Conference 2021 (repository.up.ac.za/handle/2263/82384): measures passengers waiting for the taxi 'to fill-up and depart'; BusinessTech (25 Jul 2020), 'Full taxis are a South African reality': operations run on the 'fill and go' model; Business Report / BusinessTech (2020) and Daily Dispatch: fares paid per trip (workers' taxi cost averages about R960 a month). Vehicles are 15-seaters converted to taxi standard (cars.co.za, 2013), so 'klein bus' fits. Accurate as a Grade 4 definition. Departing when full describes leaving the rank; along the route taxis also stop for passengers, which the definition does not deny.

items.bewering: vragmotor: 'n Groot voertuig wat vrag op paaie van plek tot plek ry.
items.bron: Britannica Dictionary (learnersdictionary.com/definition/truck): a truck is 'a very large, heavy vehicle' for moving goods, British 'lorry'; Wordnik / American Heritage: a vehicle for carrying goods. Afrikaans 'vragmotor' corresponds to English truck or lorry. 'Groot' matches the main dictionary sense; the definition is accurate for Grade 4.

items.bewering: goederetrein: 'n Trein wat vrag dra in plaas van mense.
items.bron: Oxford Learner's Dictionaries, 'freight train': 'a train that carries only goods' (British 'goods train'); Law Insider: a freight train is 'a Train which is not a Passenger Train'; Vocabulary.com, Dutch 'goederentrein' (the same compound). Accurate.

opsomming: All 34 claims were checked against sources and confirmed, with no contradictions and nothing uncertain; the one thing worth a person's glance is the opening frame 'look tomorrow at the road past your school, most children come on foot', which is true for South Africa as a whole (about 61-63% of learners walk) but will not match what learners see at many urban and suburban schools, so it is a choice for whoever owns the lesson, not a factual error.
